title: k-means clustering
tagline: Drop k flags on a map; everyone joins their nearest flag; each flag walks to the middle of its crowd; repeat.
history: Lloyd's algorithm, devised at Bell Labs in 1957 (published 1982); the name "k-means" comes from MacQueen in 1967.
useCases: A fast baseline before fancier clustering
whenToUse: Roughly spherical, similar-size clusters, numeric scaled features, and a k you can pick.
whenNotToUse: Non-convex shapes, very different densities, unknown k, or categorical data — reach for DBSCAN, GMM, or hierarchical.
complexity: O(n · k · i) time · converges to a local optimum (seed matters)
note: It stops at a minimum, not the minimum. Seed badly and you get a bad answer, confidently. Press reset a few times and watch it happen.

code.ruby:
def kmeans(points, k, iters: 100)
  centroids = points.sample(k)
  labels = nil
  iters.times do
    labels = points.map { |p| (0...k).min_by { |i| dist2(p, centroids[i]) } }
    new_c = (0...k).map do |i|
      cluster = points.select.with_index { |_, j| labels[j] == i }
      cluster.empty? ? centroids[i] : mean(cluster)
    end
    break if new_c == centroids
    centroids = new_c
  end
  [labels, centroids]
end
